Keep users, negatives and tie handling identical. For each dataset, compute paired user differences dᵤ = hit_new − hit_baseline; report mean difference, gains/losses and an exact McNemar test on discordant users. Bootstrap paired users within each dataset, then average the four dataset differences equally for a macro confidence interval. One changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points within a dataset, 0.125 macro points. These intervals concern user sampling conditional on fixed candidates, training seed and datasets; they exclude negative-sampling and training variability. Sampled HR can reverse full-catalog model rankings, so retain the pinned evaluator and limit claims accordingly. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

Repeated hyperparameter selection makes the winning validation score optimistic; ordinary winner-only intervals do not correct this. Log every configuration and epoch comparison, specify stopping rules and practical effect thresholds, and label results exploratory. Simultaneous paired-bootstrap intervals across a prespecified configuration set can address multiplicity, but cannot remove unrestricted adaptive-search bias. With splits fixed and test labels unavailable, independent confirmation remains unavailable during search. [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)

Proposed diagnostics: compare intact text against no-text, globally shuffled item-to-text assignments, and assignments shuffled within training-frequency bins while matching text length/missingness. Within-item token shuffling tests word order, not all semantics; masking identifiers and repeated boilerplate probes lexical shortcuts. Use matched HSTU retraining controls, each loading one checkpoint/category, never combining scores. Inference-only corruption is a sensitivity check with distribution-shift caveats. Report paired gains by train-only item-frequency bins and text availability, plus recommendation popularity and coverage. Separate naturally missing text from randomized masking. Persistence after frequency-matched shuffling weakens semantic attribution; gains concentrated in intact-text tail items strengthen it, without proving causality.
